study.question: Does preserving within-event category/brand--action/recency association before pooling improve the existing match-group model, beyond its additive means, direct counts, fixed action-age histograms and equally wide factorized cross-moment readout? Does that effect depend on semantic versus same-cardinality positional grouping of only the new readout?
study.hypothesis: Observed source limitation: the incumbent adds category, brand, action and recency embeddings before averaging within four exact target-match groups. Permuting complete (action, age) bundles within any true group preserves that mean, direct counts and its full action-age histogram for every embedding assignment, while destroying which category/brand bundle had which context. The supplied representation contains no history item IDs: content here means category and brand only. A diagonal cross moment E[C*T], C=e_category+e_brand and T=e_action+e_log2_age, can retain some of this association. The paired-minus-independent contrast is diagonal covariance E[C*T]-E[C]*E[T], not a new input or longer history. This is an algebraic representational limitation plus a provisional predictive hypothesis, not evidence that the missing association predicts clicks.

nearest_work.difference: DIN describes groupwise embedding/pooling and target-dependent weighted sums, with explicit target-behavior products in its activation unit. We instead retain the local incumbent hard-match means and add category/brand-by-context products as VALUES before pooling, contrasted with products of marginal means. No neural event scorer, new query, DIN reproduction or priority claim. The supplied baseline uses normalized attention, whereas primary DIN relaxes sum-to-one weights.

Author README explicitly limits behavior identity to category/brand/type, without item. We honor those fields. This is only a field-boundary check; the blocked full paper was not inspected and no detailed DMR mechanism difference or reproduction is claimed.

nearest_work.difference: UniDot appends explicit per-layer token dot products/Grams to a classifier to preserve second-order information around compression/fusion. Our readout uses diagonal within-event content-context products within existing fixed match groups before their information is averaged away. There is no dual bus, per-layer highway, dot-product token classifier, mutual learning, conversion-delay label or optimizer change. Second-order products and pooling are established ideas; novelty of this combination is unverified. Its reported system result does not establish transfer.

Exact supplied incumbent source was compared with candidate.py before modification. Keep its learned match pools, direct counts, observed action-age histograms, embedding tables and dormant attention allocation. Add 4*d=64 cross-moment coordinates, hence 8192 first-layer weights. Unlike the previous histogram factorial, these coordinates bind learned category/brand identities to context and distinguish a within-group context-swap collision.

study.proposed_difference: Append four 16D diagonal cross-moment vectors, scaled by a fixed shared 1/2 (unit initial coordinate variance under independent default unit-variance embedding components). For each new readout group compute BOTH observed=mean(C*T) and independent=mean(C)*mean(T), using the same embeddings and denominator max(group_size,1), then select one. Independent is the exact all-pairs empirical product, including self-pairs, not a random derangement. Cross pairing (observed vs independent) with group membership (true neither/category-only/brand-only/both vs valid-position rank partitions with identical four sizes). Change only the new readout: old pools, counts and 64 observed histogram cells remain fixed in all four cells. Empty groups are zero; missing-to-missing never matches. All four allocate 17153315 parameters, 17078688 embeddings and 74627 dense parameters with target metadata; each adds 8192 weights to the incumbent and all Model ASTs/allocation order are identical. Cost is three new small batched products and repeated existing lookups, O(B*L*d) rather than all-event-pair attention; no quadratic pair tensor is built. No input expansion, depth, auxiliary task, optimizer or training changes. The factorial controls do not rule out embedding basis, feature scale or optimization explanations; products are not asserted novel.
predictions: Algebraic positive control: two events within the same true-match group with content scalars C=(1,3), context T=(2,5), and then reversed T, have identical incumbent representations and identical independent moment 7, but observed moments 8.5 and 5.5 (readout scales all by 1/2). This uses complete context bundles so the observed action-age histogram is unchanged. In vector form the distinction is available when at least one learned coordinate differs in both operands.

On host first-512 diagnostics, within-true-group context reversal should preserve ancestor pool/stats/hist inputs up to floating-point tolerance; independent semantic moments should also be invariant, while paired semantic moments can change if empirical association is present. Raw singleton/empty covariance must be zero. The semantic both-match content vector is constant, so its covariance should be numerically zero, an additional structural negative control. Rank controls need not satisfy semantic reversal invariance or zero both-slot covariance.

Predictive screening prediction: content_paired_match exceeds content_independent_match in full-population validation ROC-AUC. A gap >=.0002 plus improvement over incumbent is a predeclared practical trigger for paired-seed follow-up, not a significance threshold. Smaller consistent gaps can justify a diagnostic follow-up if measured cost is small; no single seed establishes statistical significance.

Secondary semantic-locality prediction: [paired_match-independent_match] > [paired_rank-independent_rank] with the incumbent unchanged. This interaction would suggest relevance partitioning of the NEW moment readout helps; a pairing effect in both groupings instead suggests generic within-event association. No source-method mechanism is thereby validated.

Report Logloss, full-protocol parameter/memory/train/wall/inference costs and host fixed slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Earlier incumbent improvements were uneven: versus r0005, its history_1_16 AUC fell .5776149853 to .5722919814 and history_17_64 .5963457775 to .5928623917 while history_gt64 rose .6194269111 to .6201370729. The small/empty slices are exploratory and cannot outweigh the primary metric without predeclared justification. No new split, selection over test or changed history window.
falsifiers: If ancestor inputs change materially under within-true-group context reversal, or semantic independent moments change beyond roundoff, the proposed diagnostic or implementation is wrong; withhold mechanism interpretation, retain failed costs and repair only in a new counted attempt. Numerical diagnostic checks are not performance evidence.

If paired and independent readouts improve equally over the incumbent, added separable nonlinear capacity or easier optimization explains the gain at least as well as retained association. If paired loses while covariance is nonzero, this implementation has not shown predictive utility; the source collision remains mathematically real.

If association is negligible on the authorized diagnostic batch, the predictive premise lacks local activation evidence; do not label the mechanism supported merely because a larger model wins. If gains reverse across paired seeds, report unstable preliminary evidence. If the rank factorial has equal or larger pairing effect, reject the semantic-specific extension while retaining any generic association hypothesis.

An unsuccessful finite diagonal learned-product implementation does not rule out all event-granularity representations. No outcome here establishes global novelty, causal production validity, or benefit on unavailable item identifiers or older-than-supplied events.
alternative_explanations: Additional first-layer capacity versus incumbent, feature variance depending on group size, degree-two basis/regularization, and changed gradient flow can affect optimization independently of information preservation. Same parameter count and allocation within the factorial address gross capacity/initialization, not these differences. Diagnostics report raw observed/independent RMS and covariance; a future fixed-scale or replacement comparison would be needed for stronger attribution.

Rank replacement retains exact sizes but uses deterministic supplied order and changes groupwise content/context marginals; it is not a randomized no-semantics control. Rank effects may reflect recency/order composition. No isolated grouping claim from a single diagonal comparison; interpret paired contrasts and factorial interaction.

Embeddings are trained jointly and content sums still collapse category versus brand; diagonal products miss off-diagonal and higher-order effects. Within both-match groups content is constant, so the main incremental information must come from other groups. Missing fields, hashing and coarse identities limit what association can survive.

Many previous validation-guided rounds, one training seed, correlated impressions per user, and exploratory first-512 diagnostics can produce winner selection bias. Existing slices contain shared users; no impression-iid confidence claims. Reserve paired repetitions and user-cluster bootstrap only if host permits paired predictions; otherwise disclose unavailable intervals.

Source cards concern other data/tasks and training regimes. Prior declared consideration and executed variants do not measure the causal value of external knowledge. No disabled personal source, new labels, extra history, closed assessment input or external system performance is imported as local evidence.
